newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African mercenaries ready to help Mobutu- paper.
newsitem.headline: S.African mercenaries ready to help Mobutu- paper.

text.p: South African mercenaries are on standby to help Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko hold the capital Kinshasa if rebels try to take control of it, a South African newspaper reported on Saturday.

The Afrikaans-language Beeld, quoting anonymous sources, said more than 500 mercenaries, not linked to the well-known Pretoria-based Executive Outcomes group, were in Zaire preparing to intervene on behalf of the ailing Mobutu.
It said that another group of mercenaries from South Africa was alleged to be working in Zaire alongside Ugandan troops loyal to Zaire's rebel leader Laurent Kabila.

South African foreign affairs officials, while emphasising they were unable to confirm the story, said the government was extremely concerned by reports of South Africans working as mercenaries abroad and wanted to clamp down.
"It's counter-productive and undermines the work being done by different governments in trying to resolve the situation politically," one official told Reuters.

"The government has instituted legislation to regulate South African mercenaries being recruited to work abroad by private companies. It should be tabled in parliament during the present session of parliament," he said. Parliament sits until the end of October.
